strategyReview: Weekend Hyperliquid funding reversion long remains the engine's strongest live signal, delivering 75% win rate across 279 trades and consistent realized profits; one-touch NO edge selling on Polymarket has perfect 4/4 live wins and large average returns, while P/C ratio extreme signals maintain healthy win rates. The notable failure mode is forward-testing of recently promoted shadow-mined hypotheses—particularly the GOLD heatmap NO cluster and the AMZN perp/spot convergence family—which are losing in real-time despite strong in-sample statistics, indicating overfit to a short historical window. BTC PM IV expansion/reversion signals have also degraded as absolute IV thresholds lost relevance, underscoring the need for regime-relative conditions. Most cross-asset momentum confirmations (HYPE→BTC) are failing outright, suggesting the risk-on proxy logic is unsound in current market conditions.

failureClusters.theme: Overfit one-touch NO edge clusters on specific assets
failureClusters.evidence: GOLD one-touch NO edge heatmap variant H-534 has 0% win rate (0/14 scorable, 0/35 overall), and its shadow parent family averages 44% win with recent GOLD/ETH losses; multiple FIND-derived gold NO hypotheses are failing.
failureClusters.recommendation: Kill the GOLD heatmap family and any hypothesis relying solely on a static underlying-cap edge threshold. Only promote one-touch NO edges when accompanied by regime-relative volatility conditions, smart-flow stance, or confirmatory macro context.

failureClusters.evidence: Primary variant H-005 has 0% win; funding remained pinned at 5.5% rather than normalizing, and 83 tests became unscorable due to unevaluable conditions. The convergence logic did not produce the expected perp/stock move.
failureClusters.recommendation: Disable the AMZN convergence family unless a radically different mechanism is proposed—e.g., requiring a large funding decline from an elevated level combined with deeply negative basis. Consider permanent kill.

failureClusters.theme: Static IV thresholds for PM expansion/reversion break down
failureClusters.evidence: H-001 (BTC PM IV expansion) win rate collapsed to 30% (3/10) after early wins; cross-asset IV compression cluster 0/8. Fixed thresholds like btc_pm_iv < 46 no longer identify meaningful dislocations.
failureClusters.recommendation: Shift to percentile or z-score-based compression (e.g., bottom 20% of 30d range) coupled with directional trend or funding exhaustion filters to isolate genuine volatility expansions.

failureClusters.theme: Shadow-mined weekend funding asset variants lack weekend context
failureClusters.evidence: H-539 (CBRS) and H-537 (AAPL) show 50% and 45% win rates with high whipsaw; funding oscillated unpredictably without weekend-day filtering. The original shadow mining likely captured temporary regimes.
failureClusters.recommendation: Add explicit day_of_week weekend constraints and deeper funding extremes (< -20%) to reduce noise, or rely on the aggregated weekend reversion signal which already operates profitably across many assets.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of AMZN funding convergence: instead of waiting for near-zero basis after a flip, short AMZN perp when funding is elevated (≥15%) and basis is deeply negative (≤ -0.5%), expecting funding to decline and perp to depreciate.
newHypotheses.prediction: AMZN perp price will decline >2% within 5 days as funding normalizes lower.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of CBRS weekend funding reversion shadow: require extreme weekend funding (< -20%) on Saturday or Sunday, isolating the genuine weekend funding crash episodes.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS funding will normalize upward within 2 days, and spot price will increase >2%.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of AAPL weekend funding reversion shadow: apply weekend-only filter and deeper funding threshold (< -20%) to capture true weekend funding squeezes.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL funding will revert upward within 2 days, leading to >2% spot gain.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of BTC PM IV expansion: replace absolute IV thresholds with regime-relative compression (PM IV z-score ≤ -1.5) while options IV remains elevated (>40), retaining the thesis that compression leads to spot expansion but adding a regime filter.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot moves >2% in absolute terms within 3 days as compression releases.

newHypotheses.description: Fade rich PM IV on upside one-touch NO contracts: when PM IV exceeds options IV by ≥10 vol points, short spot via selling YES on those touch-high contracts.
newHypotheses.prediction: Spot price will decline >2% within 7 days as PM IV premium erodes.

newHypotheses.description: Rich PM IV near-expiry NO fade: tighten the rich-IV signal to contracts expiring within 30 days, capturing faster mean reversion.
Smart-flow fade on upside touch: when smart wallets show a short- or flat-stance on YES contracts and there is at least 3pt sell-YES edge, short the spot.
newHypotheses.prediction: Spot price declines >1.5% within 5 days as smart-money positioning dominates.

hypothesisReviews.observation: All 14 forward tests resulted in gold spot moving less than 2% or in the opposite direction, despite a persistently positive underlying-cap edge. The signal did not translate into directional price moves, likely because gold's short-term moves are driven by macro flows rather than PM contract mispricing.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying-cap edge on gold upside touch contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Funding rate remained pinned at 5.5% for several days instead of normalizing downward; the basis stayed near zero, removing any incentive for further convergence. The thesis that positive funding with near-zero basis signals impending perp underperformance is disproven.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Positive AMZN funding with near-zero basis portends perp underperformance and basis normalization that completes the arbitrage.

hypothesisReviews.observation: CBRS funding exhibited high whipsaw (e.g., 32.9%→76.8% win, then 232.8%→-124.5% loss) without consistent normalization. The hypothesis lacked weekend-day filtering, causing it to trigger on non-weekend episodes where funding behavior differs.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative weekend CBRS funding reliably normalizes to less negative levels within 2 days without requiring explicit weekend context.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL funding similarly oscillated; several tests saw further negative moves. The moderate -10% threshold captured too many noisy episodes, and the absence of a weekend filter diluted the signal's edge.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative weekend AAPL funding rapidly normalizes, leading to a >2% spot gain without additional regime conditions.

hypothesisReviews.observation: After two early wins in late July, the fixed PM IV threshold (<46) became irrelevant as BTC PM IV stayed above that level or the ratio condition did not trigger. The last six tests all failed, indicating the signal captured a temporary regime that no longer exists.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: PM IV underpricing options IV by >8% (with absolute PM IV below 46) reliably leads to >2% absolute spot move within 3 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: All attempts at using HYPE OI stability and spot above SMA as confirmation for a BTC long failed, with BTC moving down ~1.6% each time. The risk-on proxy logic does not hold in the current fragmented market environment.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC above short-term trend with HYPE spot above SMA and OI stable confirms a >2% BTC long move over 3-7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: OIL one-touch NO edge heatmap variant continues to perform flawlessly with 100% win rate over 10 shadow tests, confirming that the edge-based signal for OIL is robust and may be ready for promotion when its shadow-test bar clears.
BTC PM IV regime-relative compression signal (using percentile-based conditions) is showing promise with a 67% win rate over 16 tests, supporting the shift away from absolute thresholds.

journalEntry: Tonight's review reinforces that the weekend funding reversion long and one-touch edge selling on OIL/BTC remain our live anchors. The GOLD heatmap NO cluster is killed, and AMZN convergence is terminal. We are shifting BTC IV signals to z-score-based compression and adding weekend filters to per-asset funding shadows. Six FIND-authored hypotheses enter shadow testing, targeting rich PM IV and smart-flow fade setups. Parameter stop losses tightened for underperforming funding and LLM hypothesis signals to limit drawdowns.
